thesis: T. Rowe Price Group (Nasdaq: TROW). Q3 2026 10-Q (0001113169-26-000005, filed 2026-10-29) and earnings release (Exhibit 99.1): net revenues 2,004.9M vs 1,893.5M (+5.9%), 9M 5,769.3M vs 5,380.7M; operating income 769.8M vs 643.2M (9M 1,990.8M vs 1,717.8M); net income attributable 612.3M vs 646.1M in Q3 (9M 1,742.5M vs 1,641.8M); diluted EPS 2.79 vs 2.87 (adjusted 2.86 vs 2.81). Net income fell because investment gains dropped to 32.3M from 161.2M and consolidated products swung to losses. AUM 1,862.7B at 9-30 (1,775.6B at year end). Net client flows Q3 -28.3B, 9M -48.5B (equity -61.7B 9M; fixed income +11.5B; alternatives +4.8B). Effective fee rate 37.8 bps vs 39.1 bps a year ago, mix shifting to lower fee products. Headcount 7,640, down 2.4%; adjusted expenses +5.8% in Q3. Cash 3,774.3M, discretionary investments 933.0M, no corporate debt line (403.8M debt sits inside consolidated investment products). TTM (FY2025 + 9M26 - 9M25): revenue 7,703.4M, net income attributable 2,187.8M, OCF 1,866.2M, capex 267.8M, FCF 1,598.4M. Shares 213,325,929 (cover 2026-10-27), close 108.93 gives market cap 23.24B: 10.6x TTM, FCF yield 6.9%, net cash about 4.7B gross before consolidated products (aggregator net cash 2.93B). TTM dividends paid 1,141.0M (71% of FCF); 9M dividends 856.5M plus buybacks 500.9M is 81% of 9M FCF 1,683.8M. Market view: a melting ice cube of active equity outflows; price assumes continued outflows and fee compression. What would differ: market-driven AUM growth (+5% YTD) is offsetting outflows, expenses are being managed, and fixed income and alternatives are growing. Cheap on earnings, but the cheapness is the market pricing real structural outflows. Peer update 2026-11-16 (stockanalysis.com, 2026-11-13 closes, one aggregator origin): TROW 10.6x trailing against BEN 18.3x trailing (fwd 11.15, EV/EBITDA 10.2, FCF yield 4.4%, yield 3.7%) and IVZ forward 9.2x (trailing n/a on losses, FCF yield 14.0%, EV/EBITDA 8.1). TROW is cheaper on trailing earnings, in line on forward; AMG, APAM and own history not compared.
counterthesis: Equity outflows of 61.7B in nine months, rising to 25.6B in Q3 alone, and fee rate decline (39.1 to 37.8 bps) mean revenue growth depends on market levels; a 20% market drop would cut revenue quickly with 38 to 40% margins on a mostly fixed cost base. Q3 net income and EPS fell year over year; adjusted EPS grew only 1.8%. Adjusted expenses rose 5.8% while headcount fell, with higher bonus accrual. Cash flow includes consolidated investment product effects and seed investments; TTM OCF is a reported figure not adjusted for those. Dividend plus buybacks absorb 81% of FCF; 4.8% yield is attractive but only if flows stabilize. Passive and ETF share gains, fee compression and competitor moves are structural risks, and the Q3 loss of the multi-asset category (-7.6B) shows outflows are broadening. Peers (BEN, IVZ, AMG, APAM) and own-history multiples were not read; MD&A, legal proceedings and risk factors in the 10-Q were not read; the 8-K of 2026-11-10 is unread.
invalidation: Thesis fails if net outflows keep accelerating beyond about 25 to 30B per quarter, the fee rate falls well below 37 bps, operating margin drops below 35%, or the dividend stops being covered by free cash flow.
